title: Short Stuff: The Number 23
summary: Short Stuff episode on the obsession with the number 23. The hosts discuss the 2007 Jim Carrey film The Number 23 and Michael Jordan's number 23 (an homage to his older brother's number 45... as close as he could get to half of 46) and later athletes who wore it, including David Beckham at Real Madrid. They trace the cult fascination to William S. Burroughs, who reportedly heard of a flight 23 crash and a sea captain story in Tangier in 1960, and to Robert Anton Wilson, the Illuminatus! trilogy, and Discordianism. They run through 23 coincidences found online (Darwin's Origin of Species in 1859, Kurt Cobain's birth and death years, 9/11 digits, Shakespeare's birth and death day, Julius Caesar's stab wounds), explain the birthday paradox, mention John Nash's fondness for 23 and a Life magazine cover claim, Numbers 23 in the Bible, and close with a cognitive explanation: the brain's pattern-seeking tendency.
topics: Kurt Cobain birth and death numbers

segments.title: Opening banter and the Number 23 film
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the number 23 and the 2007 Jim Carrey movie The Number 23, and discuss whether the film is worth watching.

segments.title: Michael Jordan and the number 23 in sports
segments.summary: Jordan wore 23, reportedly as close as he could get to half of 46, his older brother's number. Other athletes such as LeBron James and David Beckham at Real Madrid later wore 23 as a tribute.

segments.title: William S. Burroughs and the origin of the obsession
segments.summary: Barnaby Rogerson's book traces the obsession to William S. Burroughs, who reportedly in 1960 in Tangier heard a sea captain named Clark say he had no accidents in 23 years, then heard of a Flight 23 crash in Florida. The hosts note the story has many holes, and that Burroughs was an influential underground figure.

segments.title: Robert Anton Wilson, Illuminatus trilogy and Discordianism
segments.summary: Burroughs's friend Robert Anton Wilson co-wrote the Illuminatus trilogy, which draws on the number 23 and on Discordianism, a parody religion where 23 is a holy number. The hosts say this combination likely fed the cult-like fascination.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Break before returning to more 23 coincidences.

segments.title: Coincidences involving 23
segments.summary: Examples from online pages: Darwin's Origin of the Species (1859) adds to 23; Kurt Cobain's birth (1967) and death years add to 23; 9/11 digits add to 23; Shakespeare born and died on April 23 in different years; Julius Caesar reportedly stabbed 23 times... the hosts note Caesar was stabbed three times in detailed reports.

segments.title: The birthday paradox
segments.summary: With 23 people in a room there is about a fifty percent chance two share a birthday, because each person can be compared with every other person, producing many more comparisons than 23. The hosts admit the math is hard to follow but it is well proven.

segments.title: Star Wars, John Nash, and Bible references to 23
segments.summary: Princess Leia's cell in the first Star Wars film is block AA-23, and George Lucas's THX 1138 contains a 23 reference. John Nash, the mathematician from A Beautiful Mind, called 23 his favorite prime number and claimed to appear on a Life cover as Pope John XXIII. Numbers 23 in the Bible; Samuel Morse's first telegraph message 'What hath God wrought' is Numbers 23:23.

segments.title: Pattern seeking and why 23 seems special
segments.summary: Hosts argue 23 is not inherently special; many numbers from one to thirty could be assigned meaning. Cognitive psychologists say the brain is a pattern detector that forces meaning onto random events, the way people notice the clock at 11:11.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode, with a joke about 23 chromosomes, and the standard Stuff You Should Know sign-off.
